schema.description: Knowledge graph for Information Theory and Entropy

nodes.name: Shannon Entropy
nodes.description: Shannon entropy, the average number of bits needed to describe a random variable's outcome, quantifying its inherent uncertainty.

nodes.name: Joint and Conditional Entropy
nodes.description: Joint entropy measuring the uncertainty of several variables together, and conditional entropy measuring remaining uncertainty given another variable.

nodes.name: Mutual Information
nodes.description: Mutual information quantifying the reduction in uncertainty about one variable gained from observing another, the information they share.

nodes.name: Kullback-Leibler Divergence
nodes.description: Kullback-Leibler divergence, the relative entropy measuring the inefficiency of assuming one distribution when another is true; non-negative and asymmetric.

nodes.name: Data Processing Inequality
nodes.description: The data-processing inequality stating that processing a signal cannot increase the mutual information it carries about a source.

nodes.name: Asymptotic Equipartition Property
nodes.description: The asymptotic equipartition property, showing long sequences fall into a typical set of nearly equal probability, underpinning the coding theorems.

nodes.name: Kraft Inequality
nodes.description: The Kraft inequality giving the necessary and sufficient condition on codeword lengths for a uniquely decodable prefix code to exist.

nodes.name: Shannon Source Coding Theorem
nodes.description: Shannon's source coding theorem establishing entropy as the fundamental limit on the average rate of lossless data compression.

nodes.name: Huffman Coding
nodes.description: Huffman coding, a greedy algorithm building optimal prefix-free codes that minimise expected codeword length for known symbol probabilities.

nodes.name: Discrete Memoryless Channels
nodes.description: Discrete memoryless channels modelling noisy transmission where each output depends only on the current input via fixed transition probabilities.

nodes.name: Channel Capacity
nodes.description: Channel capacity, the maximum mutual information over input distributions, defining the highest rate of reliable communication.

nodes.name: Shannon Channel Coding Theorem
nodes.description: Shannon's channel coding theorem proving that reliable communication is achievable below capacity and impossible above it.

nodes.name: Differential Entropy
nodes.description: Differential entropy extending entropy to continuous random variables as an integral, with properties differing from the discrete case.

nodes.name: AWGN Channel
nodes.description: The additive white Gaussian noise channel, a continuous model where transmitted signals are corrupted by independent Gaussian noise.

nodes.name: Shannon-Hartley Theorem
nodes.description: The Shannon-Hartley theorem giving the capacity of a bandlimited AWGN channel as a function of bandwidth and signal-to-noise ratio.
